_comment: Output token limit of one backend call, replayed through _shared/lua/llm/request_plan/token_budget.lua by the macOS and Linux runners. A call returning one prediction keeps the base budget; a batch call returning per_call predictions gets per_call * (base + 5), the five being a variant's numbering and separator. Linux used per_call * base (no overhead) before this corpus: a deliberate convergence to the macOS and Windows rule, so a batch of three is no longer cut short on Linux. retry adds the retry policy's extra tokens. expect_error is a substring of the message the plan must raise.

drivers.windows: Not ported yet: prediction_exec.ahk caps the batch at max*n+5*n already, so it should call a port of for_call and replay every vector; its retry adds the retry policy's extra tokens the same way.

differences.batch_overhead: Linux gave a batch of n variants n*base tokens; it now gives n*(base+5) as macOS and Windows do. Convergence, written reason: the five tokens are the numbering and separator each variant spends, and without them the last variant of a batch could be cut short on Linux only.

vectors.expect_error: base_tokens must be a whole number from 1
per_call must be a whole number from 1
extra_tokens must be a whole number from 0
